items.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: And I mean I’m just saying he didn’t call everybody in the band and said do you want to hear the — you know what I mean?

ctx.x: Yeah, yes, yes, yes, yes. I took my kids, my second wife and the two kids, Adrienne and Paul, and Paul was the little one. And we took them down to Atlantic City. We were playing there, to have them meet Louis Armstrong. So they came up on the stage, you know I took them back stage, and my daughter said, “it’s nice to meet you Mr. Armstrong.” She’s the older one, she was very cute and darling. And my son Paulie must have been five or something like that. And Paul puts out his left hand because he was so ambiguous…

made some records with Pops. And he had a little phonograph. He always traveled with a phonograph, and enjoyed demos of the records. And he called me on the phone and he says, we’re in the same motel, and he says, “you want to hear the record we made?” I said, “yeah, yeah.” I said, “I’ll send up Paul, my son.” And I mean I’m just saying he didn’t call everybody in the band and said do you want to hear the — you know what I mean? It was like, so I sent Paul up, and God 45 minutes, what happened to him, did he get…
Gee that’s a neat story. Well you said in a little note you wrote to me, you said as far as your own career right now, you said thank God for Europe.
